claim.value: Flakiness, unbuildable revisions, several regressions, later fixes and interactions can invalidate binary elimination.
claim.scope: Possible failure of the elimination method under the listed complications.

provenance.rationale: The cited span expressly attributes possible invalidation to these complications.

signal_basis.value: Confident midpoint classifications determine which endpoint moves and which history is discarded under a single-transition assumption. Inconclusive results do not justify elimination, and build failures are not performance classifications; decisive results shrink the candidate interval.
signal_basis.scope: Repeated revision classification and elimination, conditional on a single transition and usable performance evidence.

provenance.rationale: These spans supply the classification rule, elimination assumption, treatment of inconclusive and unbuildable revisions, and interval-shrinking signal.
The bounded methodological limitation is supported without an unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Binary elimination requires reliable classifications and a single transition. Flakiness can undermine classification, unbuildable revisions can prevent required tests, and regressions, later fixes or interactions can defeat the single-transition assumption. Observed interval shrinkage does not ensure valid elimination when those conditions fail. The claim states a possibility, not inevitable failure or the presence of these complications.
uncertainty: The packet does not establish whether any listed complication actually occurs; that is unnecessary for this possibility claim.
